the effects of β-naphthaflavone on protein synthesis in the rabbit liver and with its effect on the induction of a cytochrome P450 mRNA.
the effect of β-naphthyoflavone on the synthesis of cytochrome-P-450 LM4.

a single injection of β-NF in corn oil causes a biphasic effect on liver protein synthesis in the rabbit.
β-naphtholavone, when injected in corn oil, induces a transient increase in the synthesis of cytochrome LM4 mRNA and a prolonged increase in the synthesis and/or stability of cytochrome 450 LM4 mRNA.

β-naphtholflavone causes changes in the polysomal poly(A+)-mRNA driven in vivo protein synthesis, and in the in vitro synthesis of cytochrome-P-450 LM4, but the effect of corn oil on polysomal poly(A)+mRNA driven in-vivo protein synthesis is greater than that of β-naphthaloflavone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

β-naphtholavone treatment of rabbits caused an increase in cytochrome P 450 LM4 mRNA levels, which was reflected by an increase in the amount of translatable cyctochrome P 450 LM 4 mRNA and a corresponding increase in the amount and rate of cytochrome p 450 LM4 synthesis.
the effect of β-naphhtoflavone on protein synthesis is due to the drug, but the induction of cyochrome P-450 LM 4 is due to both drug and oil vehicle.

β-naphthovoflavone causes a transient increase in cytochrome P450 LM4 mRNA levels in rabbit liver.
